subject: astronomy
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Neap tides (the smallest range between high and low tide) occur when:
options: The Earth is closest to the Sun
The Sun and Moon are in line
The Sun and Moon are at right angles to each other (first and last quarter)
questions.explain: At the quarter Moons the Sun and Moon pull at right angles, partly cancelling and giving neap tides.

questions.q: Which lunar phase occurs when the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun?
questions.explain: At new Moon the Moon lies between Earth and Sun, so its unlit side faces us.

questions.q: In an eclipse, the region of total shadow is called the:
questions.explain: The umbra is the dark, fully shadowed central region; the penumbra is the partial outer shadow.

questions.q: According to Newton, the gravitational force between two masses depends on distance how?
options: It increases with the square of the distance
It decreases with the square of the distance
questions.explain: Newton's law of gravitation is an inverse-square law: force falls off with the square of the distance.

questions.q: Why is the lunar surface so heavily cratered compared with most of the Earth's surface?
options: The Moon is made of softer rock
The Moon has almost no atmosphere or weather to erode or burn up impactors
The Moon attracts more meteors than Earth
questions.explain: Without an atmosphere, water or plate tectonics, impact craters on the Moon are preserved for billions of years.

questions.q: A solar eclipse can only occur at:
questions.explain: A solar eclipse needs the Moon between Earth and Sun, which only happens at new Moon.

questions.q: The Earth's rotation on its axis is responsible for:
questions.explain: As the Earth rotates once every 24 hours, places move into and out of sunlight, giving day and night.

questions.q: One astronomical unit (AU) is defined as approximately the:
options: Distance from the Earth to the Moon
Average distance from the Earth to the Sun
Distance light travels in one year
questions.explain: An AU is the mean Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million kilometres.

questions.q: It is summer in the Northern Hemisphere when:
options: The Earth is closest to the Sun
The North Pole is tilted towards the Sun
The Earth's axis is not tilted
questions.explain: Northern summer occurs when the North Pole tilts towards the Sun, giving longer days and higher Sun.

questions.q: What is the name for the streak of light seen when a small particle burns up in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explain: A meteor is the streak of light produced as a meteoroid burns up in the atmosphere; if it reaches the ground it is a meteorite.

questions.q: Most asteroids in the solar system are found in a belt located between:
questions.explain: The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.

questions.q: The phases of the Moon are caused by:
options: Clouds covering part of the Moon
Different amounts of the sunlit half of the Moon being visible from Earth
The Earth's shadow falling on the Moon
The Moon producing its own light
questions.explain: Phases occur because we see varying portions of the Moon's sunlit hemisphere as it orbits Earth.
